Five pricing mistakes early SaaS teams make
By Rohan Mehta | November 12, 2026 | 7 min read
Most early SaaS teams set a price once and never look at it again. Here are the five mistakes we see most often, and what to do instead.
1. Pricing by cost instead of value. Your costs say nothing about what a customer would pay.
2. Too many tiers. Three is plenty; five makes buyers stall.
3. Hiding the price. A 'contact us' button on a $30 product loses most visitors.
4. Never raising prices. Grandfather existing customers and raise for new ones.
5. Discounting by default. A standing 30% off trains buyers to wait.
The fix for all five is the same: talk to ten customers before you change anything.
About the author
Rohan Mehta is the cofounder of Tallyhive, a billing tool for small subscription businesses. https://tallyhive.example
Related posts: How we cut churn by a third | The annual plan playbook

Debugging flaky CI pipelines without losing your mind
Wen Liu | Nov 9, 2026
Every team has that one test that fails one run in twenty. Rerunning it until it goes green feels faster, but it hides the real problem.
Start by recording every failure with its runner, time and seed. After a week, patterns show up: shared ports, clock-dependent assertions, tests that rely on order.
Quarantine, don't delete. Move a flaky test to a separate job that can fail without blocking merges, and give it an owner and a deadline.
Finally, make reruns visible. A dashboard of rerun counts per test turns a vague annoyance into a ranked to-do list.
Wen Liu builds Pipelark, a CI insights tool. https://pipelark.example
